job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today in Geography class, we learned fascinating facts about our blue planet. I used to think clouds magically created new water, but our teacher explained that the water cycle is just a continuous movement of the same water between the earth and the atmosphere through evaporation and precipitation. We also discussed why the ocean is salty. It is not because of decaying sea creatures, but because of minerals washed from rocks into the sea over millions of years. Another interesting point was about ocean movements. I previously believed that waves carry water all the way from the middle of the ocean to the shore, but the teacher clarified that waves only cause water particles to move in a circular motion while the energy travels forward. Finally, we learned about tides. Many students thought the sun pushes the water to create tides, but the truth is that the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water is primarily caused by the strong gravitational pull exerted by the moon. It is amazing how much I misunderstood about the water around us! I feel much more informed now about how our oceans and weather systems actually work. Nature is truly a complex and beautiful system that keeps recycling itself constantly.

items.evidence: I used to think clouds magically created new water, but our teacher explained that the water cycle is just a continuous movement of the same water between the earth and the atmosphere through evaporation and precipitation.
items.q: Rain falls on a village today. Where did that water come from?
options: The same water that rose from the earth
Brand-new water that the clouds just made
Sea water that waves carried far inland
Sea water that the moon pulled up high
items.explain: The water cycle moves the same water between earth and sky; clouds do not create new water.

wrong.why: thinks waves carry water long distances
mixes up the moon's pull on tides with the water cycle

items.evidence: It is not because of decaying sea creatures, but because of minerals washed from rocks into the sea over millions of years.
items.q: Which explains why ocean water tastes salty?
options: Minerals from rocks washed in over ages
Sea creatures that died and decayed in it
Salt that rain from clouds brings daily
Salt that waves carry from mid-ocean
items.explain: Ocean salt comes from minerals washed from rocks over millions of years, not decaying sea creatures.

wrong.why: thinks salt comes from dissolved sea creatures
thinks rain brings salt, ignoring the rocks
thinks waves carry water and salt from mid-ocean

items.evidence: I previously believed that waves carry water all the way from the middle of the ocean to the shore, but the teacher clarified that waves only cause water particles to move in a circular motion while the energy travels forward.
items.q: A ball floats far out at sea as waves pass under it. What happens to it?
options: It bobs in circles, staying nearly in place
It is carried along with the water to shore
It sinks as the waves pull water down
It moves only when the moon pulls it
items.explain: Waves move water particles in circles; only the energy travels forward, not the water.

wrong.why: thinks waves carry water to the shore
mixes up waves with tides caused by the moon

items.evidence: Many students thought the sun pushes the water to create tides, but the truth is that the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water is primarily caused by the strong gravitational pull exerted by the moon.
items.q: Why does the sea at a beach come up high and then go back each day?
options: The moon's gravity pulls on the ocean water
The sun's heat pushes on the ocean water
The waves carry ocean water to the shore
The rain from clouds adds ocean water daily
items.explain: Tides, the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water, are mainly caused by the moon's gravitational pull.

wrong.why: thinks the sun pushes water to make tides
thinks waves carry water to the shore

items.evidence: Nature is truly a complex and beautiful system that keeps recycling itself constantly.
items.q: Water evaporates from a pond on a sunny day. What happens to that water?
options: It returns to the earth later as rain
It is lost from the Earth for good
It stays up in the sky as clouds forever
It is changed into new and different water
items.explain: Nature keeps recycling itself; evaporated water rises to the sky and falls back as precipitation.

wrong.why: thinks used water is gone forever
thinks the cycle stops at evaporation
